goal.objective:
`src/cli.js` is the program; how the work is split across other files under `src/` is up to you. It takes exactly one argument, `rounds` or `tally`, and reads an election from standard input. Split the input on newlines and drop the empty tail a trailing newline leaves. Trim each line; ignore it when it is empty or begins with `#`; otherwise split it on runs of whitespace. Exit 0 whenever the election parses.

The line `candidates <name>...` declares the field. It must appear exactly once, before any ballot, and must name at least one candidate; a name is one or more of the characters `A` to `Z`, `a` to `z`, `0` to `9`, `_` and `-`, and no name may repeat. The line `ballot <count> <candidate>...` records `count` identical ballots ranking those candidates from most to least preferred. The count is a decimal integer of at least 1 written without a sign and without a leading zero, a ballot names at least one candidate, every name must have been declared, and no ballot may name a candidate twice. A ballot need not rank every candidate.

Count in rounds. Every candidate starts continuing. In each round every ballot counts for the first candidate on it that is still continuing; a ballot whose named candidates are all eliminated is exhausted and counts for nobody. Let the active total be the number of ballots that counted for someone. When the active total is 0 the election ends with no winner. When some candidate's count, doubled, is greater than the active total, that candidate wins and the election ends. Otherwise exactly one candidate is eliminated and another round is counted.

The candidate eliminated is the one with the fewest votes in this round. When several tie for fewest, compare them across the rounds already counted, this one included, from the first round onwards: at the first round where their counts are not all equal, keep only those with the fewest votes in that round and compare the survivors the same way from the first round again. When no round separates them, eliminate the one whose name sorts last by code point.

`rounds` prints, for each round in order, `round K: ` followed by one `<name>=<votes>` for every continuing candidate, separated by single spaces, and then `exhausted=<n>`. Candidates are listed by descending vote count, and by ascending name where counts tie. A round that eliminated someone is followed by the line `eliminated <name>`. `tally` instead prints one line, `rounds N`, holding how many rounds were counted. Both modes end with `winner <name>`, or `no winner` when no candidate ever reached the majority.

A failure writes one line to standard error and exits 2, having written nothing to standard output; stop at the first one. The messages are `error: usage: cli.js rounds|tally` when the argument is not exactly one of the two mode words; `error: line N: candidates must be declared once, before any ballot`; `error: line N: expected candidates <name>...`; `error: line N: invalid candidate name <name>`; `error: line N: candidate <name> is declared twice`; `error: line N: expected ballot <count> <candidate>...`; `error: line N: count must be a positive integer`; `error: line N: unknown candidate <name>`; `error: line N: candidate <name> is repeated`; `error: line N: unknown directive <word>`; and `error: no candidates`, with no line number, when the input declares none. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root. This task is also judged on inputs you do not see: a validator runs your program on its own held-back cases and compares the exit code and output byte for byte. The visible tests cover the main paths only. Implement the written specification, including every corner it states, rather than the behaviour the visible tests happen to pin down.

- `dsh-find-simplifications`: Use when working in the deepseek-harness repo to find non-obvious simplification candidates, write proposed Agent Notes or inline TODO/FIXME/XXX notes, audit or coalesce superseded Agent Notes, or fold worthwhile simplification ideas from another PR; especially for dead, duplicated, speculative, over-built, added-then-removed, or hand-rolled-where-a-dependency-exists surfaces.

Requires every same-repository dependency chain to use GitHub's official stacked-PR feature before landing so GitHub owns stack-wide rules, CI, ordering, retargeting, and merge state.
- `dsh-pre-push-checks`: Use before pushing, force-pushing, marking ready for review, or claiming checks pass on a deepseek-harness branch, and immediately after gh stack sync publishes rewritten branches, to select the smallest tests and checks that cover the outgoing or just-published diff without reflexively running the full repository suite.
- `dsh-prose-standard`: Use when writing, reviewing, restoring, trimming, or auditing prose in the deepseek-harness repo, including deciding where documentation or comments are required across Markdown, JSDoc, code and test comments, prompts, descriptions, diagnostics, and CLI or UI strings.
- `dsh-trim-cot-leakage`: Use when auditing or fixing prose that reads like a leaked reasoning transcript — dead design-session citations such as (decision N), audit item codes, or §N of uncommitted drafts; change narration such as "used to", "no longer", "this cut"; stack or review vantage ("a later PR in this stack", "rejected in review"); reviewer-addressed justifications; control-flow narration; or hedged planning residue in comments, JSDoc, docs, or Agent Notes.
- `record-browser-gif`: Record browser or Web UI interaction demos as optimized GIFs using the available built-in browser, state-based frame capture, and deterministic encoding, then publish to a dedicated assets branch when the task includes attaching the GIF to a pull request. Use when asked to make, record, or generate a GIF that demonstrates a browser workflow, and for every pull request that changes product-user-visible GUI behavior, which MUST include a GIF recorded from the pull request's real server and mode...

header.system:
You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You implement one program task in the workspace you are given, against its own test suite, and you stop when the tests pass.

The workspace is your working directory: every bash command and every file path resolves inside it, so read and edit its files by their relative paths and never search outside it.


Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

All 16 tests pass, and there's no git repo here to commit to (this workspace isn't a git checkout), so the task is just the file changes under `src/`.

Summary of the implementation:

- **`src/parser.js`** — parses stdin into `{ candidates, ballots }`, dropping the trailing empty line, trimming/skipping blank and `#` lines, and validating the `candidates`/`ballot` directives with the exact error messages and line numbers specified (declaration order, name charset, duplicate names, ballot format, count format, unknown/repeated candidates, unknown directives, and the line-less `no candidates` error).
- **`src/election.js`** — runs the instant-runoff count: per round it finds each ballot's first continuing candidate (or counts it exhausted), computes the active total, checks for a majority winner or a zero active total, and otherwise eliminates the lowest scorer — using a `breakTie` helper that replays round-by-round history from round 1, narrowing repeatedly to the historical-fewest survivors and restarting from round 1 each time it narrows, falling back to the code-point-greatest name when history never separates the tied candidates.
- **`src/cli.js`** — validates the single `rounds`/`tally` argument, reads all of stdin, calls the parser/election modules, and prints either the full per-round listing (candidates sorted by descending votes then ascending name, plus `exhausted=` and `eliminated <name>` lines) or just the `rounds N` count, finishing with `winner <name>` or `no winner`; any thrown `ElectionError` (or bad usage) writes a single `error: ...` line to stderr and exits 2 without having touched stdout.

I verified beyond the given test suite: leading-zero/zero counts, invalid name characters, extra CLI arguments, a genuine historical tie-break across multiple rounds (confirmed it eliminates by earliest-round fewest-votes then falls back to lexicographically-last name), and an all-candidates-exhausted-mid-election path — all matching the spec. `node_modules` is absent and only files under `src/` were touched.

goal.objective:
`src/cli.js` is the program; how the work is split across other files under `src/` is up to you. It takes exactly one argument, `rounds` or `tally`, and reads an election from standard input. Split the input on newlines and drop the empty tail a trailing newline leaves. Trim each line; ignore it when it is empty or begins with `#`; otherwise split it on runs of whitespace. Exit 0 whenever the election parses.

The line `candidates <name>...` declares the field. It must appear exactly once, before any ballot, and must name at least one candidate; a name is one or more of the characters `A` to `Z`, `a` to `z`, `0` to `9`, `_` and `-`, and no name may repeat. The line `ballot <count> <candidate>...` records `count` identical ballots ranking those candidates from most to least preferred. The count is a decimal integer of at least 1 written without a sign and without a leading zero, a ballot names at least one candidate, every name must have been declared, and no ballot may name a candidate twice. A ballot need not rank every candidate.

Count in rounds. Every candidate starts continuing. In each round every ballot counts for the first candidate on it that is still continuing; a ballot whose named candidates are all eliminated is exhausted and counts for nobody. Let the active total be the number of ballots that counted for someone. When the active total is 0 the election ends with no winner. When some candidate's count, doubled, is greater than the active total, that candidate wins and the election ends. Otherwise exactly one candidate is eliminated and another round is counted.

The candidate eliminated is the one with the fewest votes in this round. When several tie for fewest, compare them across the rounds already counted, this one included, from the first round onwards: at the first round where their counts are not all equal, keep only those with the fewest votes in that round and compare the survivors the same way from the first round again. When no round separates them, eliminate the one whose name sorts last by code point.

`rounds` prints, for each round in order, `round K: ` followed by one `<name>=<votes>` for every continuing candidate, separated by single spaces, and then `exhausted=<n>`. Candidates are listed by descending vote count, and by ascending name where counts tie. A round that eliminated someone is followed by the line `eliminated <name>`. `tally` instead prints one line, `rounds N`, holding how many rounds were counted. Both modes end with `winner <name>`, or `no winner` when no candidate ever reached the majority.

A failure writes one line to standard error and exits 2, having written nothing to standard output; stop at the first one. The messages are `error: usage: cli.js rounds|tally` when the argument is not exactly one of the two mode words; `error: line N: candidates must be declared once, before any ballot`; `error: line N: expected candidates <name>...`; `error: line N: invalid candidate name <name>`; `error: line N: candidate <name> is declared twice`; `error: line N: expected ballot <count> <candidate>...`; `error: line N: count must be a positive integer`; `error: line N: unknown candidate <name>`; `error: line N: candidate <name> is repeated`; `error: line N: unknown directive <word>`; and `error: no candidates`, with no line number, when the input declares none. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root. This task is also judged on inputs you do not see: a validator runs your program on its own held-back cases and compares the exit code and output byte for byte. The visible tests cover the main paths only. Implement the written specification, including every corner it states, rather than the behaviour the visible tests happen to pin down.
